title: KPI Sensitivity Scenarios — Ops Notebook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This notebook captures a compact set of KPI sensitivity scenarios and the lightweight operational playbooks we want on-hand for progressive traffic ramps (0% -> 100%) and unexpected signal-washes. It is intentionally pragmatic: short checklists, owner attributions, and measurable thresholds that map to fast decisions.

Context notes (why this exists):
- Product team wants a smaller, scenario-first artifact engineers and on-call can use during incremental traffic ramps.
- Focused on three dimensions: latency, error-rate, and business conversion signals (calls to billing, auth, embeddings throughput).
- Complement to larger launch plans — this is the "what to do now" notebook for first 72 hours of ramp and worst-case stress windows.

Quick glossary (how terms used here):
- Signal-wash: sudden transient spike in noise (e.g., upstream retries) that masks real KPIs.
- Sensitivity bucket: group of KPI shift magnitudes (low/med/high) used to pick response lane.
- Stress-response lane: procedural lane (observe, mitigate, rollback, throttle, escalate).

Primary KPIs we watch (and why):
- P95 generate latency (ms) — direct UX cost, primary SLO anchor.
- Error rate (5xx and model-runtime-exceptions) — availability signal.
- Token cost per request (mean) — immediate unit-economics impact.
- Conversion signal (feature-specific): percent of sessions that hit conversion hook X.
- Queue length / pending requests per shard — capacity pressure indicator.

Sensitivity buckets (configurable thresholds):
- Low sensitivity: P95 +10–25% baseline; Error +0.5–1.5pp; Token cost +3–7%
- Medium sensitivity: P95 +25–60%; Error +1.5–4pp; Token cost +7–20%
- High sensitivity: P95 >+60% OR Error >4pp OR sustained token cost +20%

For each bucket we define a primary action set and secondary mitigations.

Scenario matrix (short actions):
1) Low sensitivity (first 10% traffic increment)
   - Owner: release lead (Maya) + oncall-sre
   - Observe: 0–30m rapid checks (dashboard delta), sample traces for tail events
   - Primary: continue ramp, enable 1m extended trace sampling for affected model shards
   - Secondary: reduce batch max size by 10% (if latency origin) or enable KV prefix caching on path X
   - Escalation if persists >45m -> move to Medium lane

2) Medium sensitivity (during 10–50% ramp or post-traffic spike)
   - Owner: eng-plat lead (Riley) + product-ops triage
   - Observe: 15m and 60m rolling windows; add token-cost sampling for top-10 routes
   - Primary: enact partial throttling (limit new sessions to baseline QPS +20%), switch heavier model variant to cheaper quantized variant where quality budget allows
   - Secondary: temporarily disable non-critical post-processing (reranker, extra embeddings) for affected routes
   - Escalation: if KPI not stabilized in 30m -> follow High lane

3) High sensitivity (severe regressions or sustained cost spike)
   - Owner: Eng Director on-call + Product Ops lead
   - Primary: immediate rollback to previous model version or traffic split fallback to region/variant with verified profile
   - Fallback: apply global short-circuit: route new requests to Hosted API compatibility pool (reserve) while we diagnose
   - Communication: notify CS and AP teams; open incident bridge; publish one-pager to #prodops-incident

Operational checklist (72-hour ramp template):
- T-minus 36h: final runway check (capacity reservations, dedicated GPU pools confirmed) — owner: product-ops
- T-minus 6h: pre-ramp smoke test (10k synthetic tokens across heavy routes) — owner: SRE
- Ramp start (0% -> 10%): 0–1h: watch p95, error, queue metrics every 5m; maintain log sampling
- Ramp (10% -> 50%): 1–6h: medium bucket responses ready; lock model variant pin for 30m windows
- Ramp end (50% -> 100%): 6–24h: revert non-critical toggles; confirm conversion signals within expected band
- Post-ramp (24–72h): run 24h cost reconciliation and compare token-cost to projection; file any quality regressions in repo/tests

Quick owners & contact table (formatted as lines):
- Product-ops owner: Maya Thompson (maya@redwood.ai)
- Engineering platform: Riley Chen (riley@redwood.ai)
- SRE / oncall: Diego Morales (diego@redwood.ai)
- Solutions / CS liaison: Priya Rao (priya@redwood.ai)

Minimal incident bridge agenda (first 30m):
1) One-line impact statement + scope (who/which region/routes)
2) Live metrics snapshot (P95, 5xx, queue length, token-cost delta)
3) Active mitigations in place and next step plan (rollback, throttle, variant-split)
4) Owner assignments (who acts in next 10m, 30m, 60m)
5) External comms template ready (CS note + status page blurb)

Comms templates (short):
- Internal: "We are currently observing elevated latency and partial errors on [route]. Triage in progress; mitigation lane: partial traffic split to fallback variant. Next update in 15m. Owner: [owner]."
- Customer-facing (CS): "We've detected a service disruption for [feature]. We're routing affected requests to a verified fallback to restore service while we investigate. No data loss expected. Status: investigating."

Post-incident minimal auto-steps (to be scripted):
- Generate cost delta report for incident window (tokens, GPU hours) -> attach to incident
- Snapshot model input samples for failing requests -> store in secure bucket (PHI review if applicable)
- Create regression ticket with against the acceptance test harness and flag for applied-ml review

Open questions (work-in-progress):
- What is our firm threshold to auto-switch model variant under token-cost pressure? (ops currently says +15% sustained for 20m; product wants 30m)
- Which routes are allowed non-critical processing to be disabled? Need final owner list from product feature guild.
- Can we script the fallback split in the orchestration layer as a single toggle? If not, manual steps are too slow.

Quick links / short pointers for next steps:
- Review confluence: PRODOPS-527 (sensitivity matrix) — action: align +15% vs +20% threshold by next weekly sync
- Jira: PRODOPS-843 — follow-up automation for scripted fallback split (owner: Riley)
- GH PR: infra/traffic-split-automation #314 (blocking test fixes)

Notes to self (short, messy):
- sample-size for token-cost calc: 1k requests across top 3 routes gives stable mean
- prefer P95 over P99 for initial ramp decisions (P99 is noisy and invites premature rollback)
- keep communication short; customers hate long incident posts without ETA

Appendix: Minimal metrics payload we show on dashboard (text table)
- metric_name | window | action_threshold | owner
- p95_latency | 5m | +25% | SRE
- error_rate_5xx | 5m | +2pp | Eng-platform
- token_cost_mean | 15m | +12% | Product-ops
- queue_len_per_shard | 1m | >75% capacity | SRE

End of notebook — this is intentionally short. Use as the canonical "first-72h" response playbook.

Last updates: added medium/high lane definitions and scripted post-incident steps (2025-02-12).
